messages:
darian (newhire): hey all, trying to `docker pull registry.internal.redwood/inference-test:latest` from WSL2 on my Windows laptop but it hangs at "Downloading" forever. followed onboarding (wireguard + split-tunnel). any quick checks? :thinking:

jess: welcome darian! first quick Q: are you resolving registry.internal.redwood to a private IP? run `nslookup registry.internal.redwood` inside WSL.

darian (newhire): nslookup returns 10.8.5.12 which looks right. got a long tcp handshake though:
```
$ curl -vI http://registry.internal.redwood:5000
* Rebuilt URL to: http://registry.internal.redwood:5000/
*   Trying 10.8.5.12...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* connect to 10.8.5.12 port 5000 failed: Connection timed out
* Failed to connect to registry.internal.redwood port 5000: Connection timed out
```

liam: ok so DNS works but route or firewall likely. on WSL, split-tunnel sometimes leaves WSL using Windows DNS or Windows default route. can you `cat /etc/resolv.conf` and `ip route` in WSL?

darian (newhire): here's `/etc/resolv.conf`:
```
nameserver 10.10.0.2
search corp.internal
```
and `ip route` shows default via 172.22.112.1 dev eth0 and 10.8.0.0/16 via 10.10.10.1 dev wg0

sam: two things to try: 1) make sure Docker daemon in Windows is configured to use the WSL2 distro's network or that traffic to 10.8.5.12 is routed from Windows host into WireGuard. 2) try `curl` from Windows PowerShell to see if it's a WSL-only problem.

darian (newhire): curl from PowerShell also times out. so Windows host can't reach it either. i'm on company wifi with split-tunnel enabled.

oncall-sre: I suspect the split-tunnel policy only sends `*.internal.redwood` but the registry's vhost/port is blocked by the NGW ACL for new subnets. can one of infra check SG/NACL? tagging @sam.

sam: checking security groups and routing... (looking)

infra-bot: Created ticket NET-3121: "newhire registry access - split-tunnel / WSL routing" assigned to eng-infra.

sam: I see the registry is in a private subnet that only allows the older bastion cluster and VPC endpoints from prod-vpn. The new dev-wg peers were not added to the ALLOWED_SOURCE list after the last rotation. I'll temporarily allow your wg peer IP 10.10.5.21 for 30m, retest and then add the proper rule to the infra change list.

darian (newhire): after the SG change `curl -vI` now gets HTTP 200, and `docker pull` progresses. woo! :tada:

jess: awesome. for long-term we need a couple follow-ups: - add dev-wg peer ranges to registry SG - document WSL gotcha: Windows Docker vs WSL routing - add a note on onboarding page to check the registry during first boot. darian, mind opening a small docs PR referencing NET-3121?

darian (newhire): happy to. i'll open a PR to /docs/onboarding/network.md and paste the curl output and steps that fixed it. thanks everyone for the quick help!

liam: filed ENGINF-1207 to expand registry SG to dev-wg peers and ENGINF-1208 to add an automated alert when a new peer isn't in allowed list.

infra-bot: ENGINF-1207 and ENGINF-1208 created and linked to NET-3121.

oncall-sre: tagging this thread in the onboarding checklist so people hit the registry test early. :white_check_mark:
